crossRefs.note: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met…
He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
He who pleads his cause first seems right; until another comes and questions him.
“Does our law judge a man, unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?”
Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention;
See therefore, I have stretched out my hand over you, and have diminished your portion, and delivered you to the will…
But about Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.”
“I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am…
“Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”

people.name: Agrippa
people.line: Tetrarch who heard Paul's defense in Caesarea

people.name: Paul
people.line: Apostle to the Gentiles, author of many NT epistles

translations.web: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
translations.bsb: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:
translations.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
translations.asv: And Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth his hand, and made his defence:
